quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready to stop for red lights or yellow lights and watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow diamond-shaped warning sign tells you the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop completely at red traffic lights. You must also always obey police officers directing traffic, even if signs or signals say otherwise.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle when you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog crossing. Wait until they are well clear of your vehicle path. Always give blind pedestrians the right of way.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition, reduce your speed on wet roads, and avoid puddles and standing water. Do not use cruise control when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car every time you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time you drive.
questions.explanation: Every person in your vehicle must wear a seat belt at all times. In a crash, an unbelted person becomes a flying object and can hurt others in the car.

questions.question: Alcohol is the top cause of deadly car crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the number one cause of road deaths. Alcohol blurs vision and slows reaction time, making it harder to respond to danger. Even small amounts of alcohol affect driving ability.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol level and reduce alcohol's effects.
questions.explanation: Only time lets your body remove alcohol from your system. Eating, drinking caffeine, or other actions cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road with traffic moving in both directions.

questions.question: What should you do to change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn on your signal. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no one is in the lane you want to enter. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign means traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: When you signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:

options.text: You only need to signal if other traffic is nearby.
It is good practice and the law requires it.
You only need to signal while making the move, not before.
You do not need to signal if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is good practice and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle right or left. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.

questions.explanation: Children are often unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware that children on bikes may suddenly come onto the road.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags help protect adults but can seriously hurt children. All children age 12 and under must sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: Which of these can impair your driving and lead to a DUI arrest?

options.text: Inhalants such as glue or paint

questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrup and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include depressants like tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough and cold medicines with alcohol or antihistamines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When you see an angry driver, what should you do?

options.text: Keep distance between you and them.

questions.explanation: When another driver is angry, stay away from them. Do not make eye contact or use hand gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever is safe to keep yourself away from danger.

questions.question: What do highway markings do?

options.text: They are only found in construction zones.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give information to drivers. They help you position your vehicle, show safe passing zones, and warn you about upcoming conditions.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: On long drives, stop every two hours to rest. If you get drowsy, pull off the road safely and take a nap, or find a place to stay overnight.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Slow down, move to the side to clear a path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the side to clear a path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must slow down, clear a path, and stop. Do not try to speed away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effects of alcohol.
Alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can make both substances more powerful. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine could affect you like several drinks alone would.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means drivers should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into their lane.
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign warns that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or allow other cars to merge into your lane.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on your body.
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: The most effective thing you can do to reduce injury or death in a traffic crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing a seat belt is the single best way to reduce your risk of injury or death while driving.

questions.question: You approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm. What should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly at 15 mph if no children are outside.
Drive at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Stay stopped until the arm retracts and the bus moves. This applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: You hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right side and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from behind, slow down and safely move to the right side of the road, then stop. In heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks when they obey traffic signals. Vehicles must stop for pedestrians at marked or unmarked crosswalks.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving faster than the speed limit or too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving faster than the speed limit or too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions commonly cause crashes. Always drive at legal speeds and adjust your speed for road and weather conditions.
